I live off of free games. Some say they're not as good, but that's bs. 
I think of this like 3rd person l4d with fewer options. the fact that i still play it means it's worth something.

"The first onslaugth is only the beginning"

i could have only written "try to belive!!!", with many "!!!!!!"...after all, is a f2p..
but that would not have been fair. i only think of the 200+h spent on this game, or consider, not irrelevant, that it was created by Valve probably to promote the platform (hey! they delayed half life 3 to release it!). Many clues it should worth a try, i think!...but still people seams to be skeptical.
That's the point of my review, to make those who still don't believe...to understand the truth. i'm joking :)
Anyway, to make things clear, it's not a shooter (with third person view ecc ecc..), it's a co-op / survival game, which gameplay base is third person shooting, with an high arcade component. the mean of the game is to collaborate to complete some levels, and it's incredible the lots of ways that could be accomplished. is not simply shooting (even because will not have enough ammo for that), but is pushing forward constantly planning every level's corner, and than execute it as fast as you can.
it's far more deep than one could think, and add-ons and moods add hours of further entertainment. One particular mood i feel to enlight: "Alien swarm: Reactive drop", that could be consider the official expansion. a stand alone mood of the game that takes years to be developed but finally released on steam and it's simply amazing.

Although a f2p, it's still the only one of his kind. Others try to take the formula, like helldivers for example, but still don't give the same feeling: 4 marines locked in a decompression chamber, planning, thinking, praying...and, finally, droping into the unknown!

                                                                     haskeer
